issue.title: [Bug]: `--mode=acp` sends the final answer twice (streamed deltas, then the whole message again as one chunk)

steps: Create hello.txt with these three lines: Weekend plan; Sat: market, then sort the bookshelf.; Sun: a 5 km run, then a quiet dinner.
Read hello.txt in the current directory, then summarize it in 3-4 sentences and give it a short title.
expected: The concatenated ACP message stream contains the final answer once.
defect: After streaming the answer deltas, plain ACP emits the complete answer again as one final message chunk.

fault location.explanation: emit_surface_event forwards assistant deltas and later the complete response text without tracking how much has already been sent. The shared-session observer already tracks offsets; #125 applies equivalent once-only behavior to plain ACP.

Root cause: emit_surface_event forwards assistant deltas and later the complete response text without tracking how much has already been sent. The shared-session observer already tracks offsets; #125 applies equivalent once-only behavior to plain ACP.

user_messages_from_issue: Read hello.txt in the current directory, then summarize it in 3-4 sentences and give it a short title.
_meta.notes: The second prompt is verbatim from the issue. The first turn prepares its exact hello.txt content in the initially empty workspace. Compare the last ACP chunk with the already-streamed suffix; do not rely on a final-output substring count alone.
